phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
In this problem,
two observation points are on opposite sides of a tower,
and the distance between those points is sixty meters.
Their angles of elevation are thirty degrees and forty-five degrees. We need to find the height of the tower.
To understand this easily,
draw the tower in the middle.
Take the height of the tower as
h. Let the distance of the thirty-degree point from the tower
be
x.
Since both points are on opposite sides and the total distance between them is sixty meters,
the distance of the other point becomes sixty minus
x.
Okay,
the figure is clear.
Now,
let us start with the easier angle first, which is forty-five degrees.
We know that ten forty-five degree is equal to height by distance,
and ten forty-five degree is one,
which gives us one equals h upon sixty minus x. So we have h equal to sixty minus x.
Got it?
Perfect.
Now let us use the thirty-degree angle.
We know that ten thirty degree is equal to one by root three.
So one upon root three is equal to h upon x, which gives us x equals root three h.
We already know that h equal to sixty minus x.

So after substituting and solving, we get sixty equals h times root three plus one h equals sixty upon root three plus one. And after rationalization, we get h equals thirty times root three minus one. Done and dusted. So the height of the tower is thirty times root three minus one meters. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
